- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overestimates — reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon after sharp price spikes — apply downward correction of 2–5% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price has risen sharply in recent days, forecast should not continue upward; cap growth at 1–2% per day unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — add a “reversal buffer” (e.g., -3 to -5% of peak) in forecast for days 8–15 post-peak.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if true outcome shows a sharp drop, model may not catch it until day 10+ — adjust for lag by adding 1–2 days of “delayed correction” in forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much — allow for 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast to reflect real-world noise.
